title: 49th ASEAN Summit closes, Philippines turns over chairmanship to Singapore
summary: Watch the closing ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit here

MANILA, Philippines – Leaders wrapped up the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits with a closing ceremony at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City on Tuesday, November 17.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. emphasized that challenges confronting Southeast Asian nations have become “increasingly intertwined,” as he delivered his closing remarks.

“Energy security is also economic security. Maritime stability sustains peace, trade, and livelihoods. Technology brings opportunity, but also new questions of security and governance, inclusion. And climate change knows no frontiers, testing the resilience of our communities,” Marcos said.
“Our institutions must therefore become as connected as the challenges that we face, and ultimately every member state must be able to count on ASEAN and ASEAN must be able to count on every member.”
During the ceremony, 2026 ASEAN chair Philippines also turned over chairmanship of the regional bloc for 2027 to Singapore.
“To Prime Minister [Lawrence] Wong and the people of Singapore, we have the utmost confidence. We offer our friendship and our full and complete support,” Marcos said.
In his remarks, Wong congratulated the Philippines “on a very successful ASEAN chairmanship,” and thanked Marcos “for steering ASEAN through a difficult year.”
Wong also announced that Singapore has chosen “Deeper Integration, Wider Partnerships” as the theme for its ASEAN chairmanship in 2027, the year the bloc turns 60.

“‘Deeper Integration,’ because we can do much more to realize the full potential of ASEAN. This includes strengthening our links in finance, digital technologies, and energy. We must take further steps toward a single ASEAN market, where businesses can set up and operate more seamlessly across borders, and where our people can enjoy more opportunities to work, invest, and prosper,” Wong said.

“‘Wider Partnerships,’ because ASEAN must continue to be open and and outward-looking. At a time when the world is becoming more divided, our response is to keep building bridges, to strengthen ties with our partners…and to ensure that Southeast Asia remains a region where all countries can engage and cooperate.”
The speeches were followed by musical performances from Julie Anne San Jose, Gary Valenciano, and P-pop group SB19.
